scenario: [LGRA.8.7]'s boundary: "A rule has at most 255 patterns", so rule `r` over exactly 255 patterns of `S`, bound `pat1` to `pat255`, compiles. Each binding is read in its own `where`, since an unreferenced binding is refused ([LGRA.8.6]), and none is `p<N>`, a percentile builtin's name ([LGRA.22.7]). Its patterns take the token positions 0 to 254, every one a byte can hold beside the 255 that names the candidate fact ([RDSC.4a.9.1]). PATH: `dsc.rete.lgra_8_7_index_overflows` counts the betas from the rule's terminal to its root on the lowered network and finds 255, and `dsc.encode` writes each position. Break: a compiler whose limit is lower refuses this; one that admits 256 passes its pair, LGRA.8.7_rule_256_patterns_refused.
